quest.title: Aroma of the Past
quest.description: The Knights have provided Razor with the ingredients he needs, and preparations seem to almost be complete. Head over to the Knights of Favonius Headquarters to check in on them.
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x60, Festive Fever x50, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

chapter.num: Of Ballads and Brews: Act III
chapter.title: Aroma of the Past

talks.objective: Go to the Knights of Favonius Headquarters

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Paimon wonders how Razor's "class" has been going...

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Sucrose! Wait!

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: #Honorary Knight {NICKNAME}, Paimon, please stop her!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, you scared Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's gotten the two of you so worked up?

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Sucrose and I agreed to present the wine ingredient to you together. But when she heard that Razor will be showing up, she insisted that she won't spend a moment longer here than she has to.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I—I'm not good at dealing with strangers... Anyway, as long as the ingredient gets into the right hands, that's all that matters...

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: That won't do! We worked on this together and we should present it together. I can't take credit for what you did.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: It's not about... the credit...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, so does this mean the Knights of Favonius' ingredient is a product of Bio-Alchemy?

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Yes, it's a Quadruple-Sweetness Sunsettia.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Quadruple sweetness? But aren't regular ones sweet enough as it is?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also... why a Sunsettia?

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Okay, um, let me give you the full story.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: I love the scent of wine, and after reading up on the art of wine-making, I have grasped some of the key principles.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: In short, whatever ingredients you use, it's essential to include something sweet.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: In an attempt to select the most suitable ingredient, I gathered samples of all the sweet plants and fruits I could find in the Mondstadt area. Then, I tried them all in turn and took detailed notes.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: I also factored in the differences between the same ingredient grown in different locations. For instance, Sweet Flowers from Springvale are a little sweeter than those at Cape Oath.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that sounds like a lot of work...

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: It was no problem at all. Just my duty as a Maid of Favonius!

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: The chance to source the "defender's will" on behalf of the Knights of Favonius is a huge honor for me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Noelle, your eyes are sparkling...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Paimon thinks it could be because of Lisa's brainwashing...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon, shush.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Um, anyway, I was worried that my evaluation would be too subjective if only I were involved. Thankfully, I ran into Sucrose the other day on her way out of the lab...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Oh no!

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: What is it, Sucrose?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I just remembered why I left the lab that day... I was supposed to go and fetch some lab equipment we imported recently...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh-oh... That look on your faces seems to say, you forgot all about it and have been in the lab this whole time...

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Yeah, exactly... I'm so sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: *sigh* Don't worry about it, it's my fault really. I'll go and see Marjorie about the equipment shortly. Carry on, Noelle.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Oh, okay!

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Anyway, Sucrose is a true professional when it comes to this kind of research! I showed her my list, and she made some extremely valuable suggestions...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Please, you don't need to go out of your way to compliment me...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Noelle filled me in on the background of the whole situation.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I was moved to see how seriously she took this task, even though she'd never even met Razor before. However, none of the potential ingredients she had identified were perfect candidates, in my opinion.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: What we needed was a fruit high in sugar and easily fermentable. After a final look at Noelle's list, I picked the Sunsettia sample from near Cider Lake as a basis, with a view to improving it.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Using Bio-Alchemical techniques, we were able to amplify the sweetness, then conduct a few tests to compare the results against the benchmarks...

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Watching Sucrose work on an experiment when she's in the zone blew me away! Such focus and determination...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Ah, I already said don't compliment me...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Anyway... The result of our research is the "Epsilon-Series Tetrasweet Sunsettia, Variation 63," and it's finally ready. The sweetness has been verified through rigorous testing, and the size and color are both optimal, too.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Noelle shortened the name to "Quadruple-Sweetness Sunsettia."

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, it can't be produced on a very large scale under the current conditions... but as long as we have enough for Razor.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: #{NICKNAME}... there's something else I'd like to share with you.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: Growing up... I was lucky. I was never the best at dealing with other people, but my parents never placed any expectations on me.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: They never said to me, "you need to be more sociable," or anything like that. They just said I should "do what I enjoy."

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: So, I'm well aware that... I'm one of the lucky ones.

response.speaker: Sucrose
response.text: I haven't lived Razor's life, and I can't pretend to imagine what it must have been like. So, I don't know how much it will mean coming from me, but... I truly hope that he can find happiness and spend his life doing what he loves.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Aw, Sucrose...

response.speaker: The door of the library
response.text: *click*

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Sorry. I am late again.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Teacher, forgot about the time. Kept talking, and talking.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's alright, we were just chatting. ...Whoa, déjà vu. Paimon said the exact same thing two days ago...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Wait a sec, where did Sucrose go?)

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: (Wow, she disappeared the moment he opened the door...)

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Hello! I'm Noelle, Maid of the Knights of Favonius.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Hi.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Here's our ingredient for you. Oh, but I can't take full credit for it! I had help from an alchemist, but right now, she... umm...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: She's a little busy with work.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Right, yes... it's a shame she couldn't be here to present it to you in person.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: *sniff* Smells like... potion, nectar, and Anemo Crystalfly... right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, nothing gets past your nose, does it?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: This Sunsettia is sweeter than ones I have smelled before. Klee said alchemy is amazing. It can make things better.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: That's right! I hope that this sweet fruit will help you brew the sweetest wine.

choices.text: The alchemist girl also had a message to pass on...

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: ...Thank you all.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: When she has time, I want to thank her, also.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Leave that to me! I'll figure out a way to persuade her to... ah, to not work so hard all the time, so that I can introduce you to each other!

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Okay, I will wait.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, now that we have all the ingredients, we can finally start making the wine. For that, we'll need a barrel — which, if Paimon remembers correctly, is waiting for us at the Angel's Share stand!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Bye, Noelle! We're gonna head off now.

response.speaker: Noelle
response.text: Good luck with everything. See you next time!

choices.text: "Spend your life doing what you love."
Can I have a little bite, just to taste?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! What's wrong with you?

talks.objective: Go to the Weinlesefest to make the wine pulp

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Honorary Knight, Razor, over here! Look who it is!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, it's Diona! Paimon was sure we'd run into you at The Cat's Tail stand some time, but so far, we haven't seen you all festival!

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Ooh... Traitors...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... Umm, wh—what?

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Arrrggghhh!!! I'm SO. MAD.

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Klee told me the whole story. So this bright idea was the brain child of you two, hmm? How could you? Razor is Daddy's friend... and he was a good influence... right up until YOU got him interested in wine!

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: Razor, you'd better promise me that you won't turn into one of those old boozehounds that drinks themselves silly, slumps over the bar, and bursts into tears!

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: I, uh... I don't understand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like there's been some crossed wires here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Klee, what exactly did you say to Diona?

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Ummmm... I told her that Razor's looking for his mommy with the Honorary Knight's help, and you both seemed really sad, and said you needed some wine, so maybe Diona could help...

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: But before I finished, Diona said, "Klee, say no more, I'm getting involved in this if it's the last thing I do." And... then we came here...

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... okay... Paimon doesn't even know where to start. Diona, it sounds like Klee left out a few important details in this story. Let us set the record straight...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You explain the situation to Diona...

dialogues.speaker: Diona
dialogues.text: So you're saying... Razor wants to make the same wine that his mother and father once made, so he can learn more about them? ...Hmm, you'd better not be making this up to try and pull the wool over my eyes...

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Sorry, Diona, it was all Klee's fault for not explaining it properly.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: So... are you still mad? Or can you help Razor make the wine?

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: I caught a bunch of fish for us to eat. Um... and you can pet Dodoco too if you want.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: ...I—I wasn't THAT angry.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: You were just trying to help. I understand.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: I just don't want Razor being led astray, that's all. That's why I may have raised my voice a little bit just now... Hmm, well, since none of you plan on drinking it, then I suppose I can help you just this once, despite my reservations.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: But I need you to know that I'm a mixer, not a brewer, so I'm used to working with the finished product. If you really want me to start with a bunch of raw ingredients, that's fine, but I can't make any promises about how it'll turn out...

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Yay! Diona is the best!

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Hehe.

choices.text: Don't worry, Diona, you got this!

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Hmph, bunch of flatterers. Now watch this.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Diona puts her signature mixological magic to work...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: All done! That was quick!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now we just need to find a place to store it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "We wait, wait for a windier day." ...Hmm, does that mean we need to put it somewhere exposed to the wind?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Maybe... Windrise? Very windy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep! If you say the word "windy," that's the first place on every Mondstadter's mind.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Cool, I wanna come, too!

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: I have to keep an eye on my foolish father, so I won't be joining you.

response.speaker: Diona
response.text: Klee, come and play again some other time.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: I will! I promise!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ah, what a curious coincidence meeting you here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tone-Deaf Bard? What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Well, I awoke to the most magnificent aroma in the air. After following the sweet scent of fresh fruit to its source, this is where I ended up.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Yeah, the fruit are super fresh and super-duper sweet! I can smell it as well!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's another reason, isn't there?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Yes. Oh ah, I remembered something important. Something that you have to do before sealing the barrel and burying it in the ground.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: What? We missed something!?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Razor, do you still remember the scent of that half-bottle of Thousand-Wind Wine? I believe there was a hint of bitterness in there?

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Yes, there was.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hahaha, and with very good reason, too. The source? ...This.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dandelion Seeds?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: You're familiar with Dandelion Wine, right? Well, the people of Mondstadt believe that the wind can bring back the soul, and also preserve memories.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Dandelion Seeds are like living gemstones, formed from the first wisps of wind in the year. People add them to the mix at the last second as a way of capturing the wind in the very moment that the barrel is sealed.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: The memory of that moment is then stored in the wine, for all time.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: So, Thousand-Wind Wine is the original Dandelion Wine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: That's so cool! So now our story will be made into wine, too!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: As for why it always has a different scent... Well, that's because people have the freedom to include whatever ingredients they want, hehe~

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: What is it, Razor? Whatcha thinkin' about?

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: In mother and father's wine, I can smell Dandelion Seeds, but I don't know what else.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: In my wine, there is a lot of... friendship.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: I still don't understand my mother and father, but... I still have you, and everyone else.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Everyone has done so much for me.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Varka, Teacher, Klee, Bennett, Uncle Brown Cat, cold lady, grown-up with fake smile...

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Grey tough girl, person that smells like Anemo Crystalfly, Uncle Browncat's daughter...

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: #Green bard, Paimon, and {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: I remember everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Making wine... is hard work.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Making this wine needed everyone, working together.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Hard work with friends... not so hard after all.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: I'm... I'm so happy.

choices.text: We are all glad to help.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Thank you.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Friends... are also lupical.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Whether I'm human, or I'm wolf... it doesn't matter. From now on, all of us are together.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: When I grow up, we will come back here. And we will open this wine... together.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: What a magnificent monologue. Even as a bard, I don't feel like there's anything else to add.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: All that remains now is to bury the barrel and wait, wait for the fruit to ferment.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The group buries the barrel in the ground...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're finally done. Paimon feels like a celebration is in order!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If Paimon remembers correctly, tomorrow should be Windcoming Day, right?

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Wow! The Anemo God is coming home!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Hahaha, that reminds me — I haven't memorized the song for the toasting ceremony yet. I'd better get back. Friends, I shall see you all tomorrow.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Get a good night's sleep tonight. Wait for the whisper of the gentle breeze to rouse you tomorrow morning, then come and enjoy a performance by the greatest bard to ever grace the streets of Mondstadt.

choices.text: It makes us happy to see you happy.

talks.objective: Go to the venue to attend the toasting ceremony

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, so many people have shown up to welcome the Anemo Archon. ...Huh? Why is everyone crowded around the Angel's Share stand?

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Tradition holds that the finest wine of the Weinlesefest only goes on sale after the Anemo Archon has tasted it at the toasting ceremony. Everyone's waiting in line for the big moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, so welcoming the Anemo Archon back is just a means to an end for them, huh... What about you, Lisa? Are you here for Razor?

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Yes, I was still feeling a little concerned about him. But I just spoke with him, and he tells me that the wine-making went very smoothly. Ah, such a relief... A glass of the festival's finest will go down smoothly now, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you too, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Lisa
dialogues.text: Hehe. Razor and the others are over there. You should go say hi.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Hey hey, there you are!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, what's with all these bottles? Selling your own home brew now?

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Haha, these are for Razor, from us!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Mommy said that everyone is welcoming the Anemo God today, and we need to give him some wine. If the Anemo God likes the wine, he'll turn into the wind and bless everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: We want the Anemo God to be happy so he helps Razor. Oh, Honorary Knight, look what Albedo let me borrow.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: This bottle is from my dads. Luckily I managed not to break it on the way here... It's just for show, though, I have to give it back to them afterwards.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Mommy said that the Anemo God can drink a looot of wine. She said if he wanted to, he could drink the whole of Cider Lake in one big gulp!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: So... d'you think we have enough between these and the wine Razor's parents left behind?

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Ahh, green bard.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ahem... Everyone, I am greatly honored to be able to be here today. I have been invited by Acting Grand Master Jean of the Knights of Favonius to perform a piece for everyone: "Thousand-Wind Wine."

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: It is some of the finest verse I know. I dedicate it to the wind, and to everyone here with us today:

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text:
"Fill up the barrels and store them away,
Then wait, wait for a windier day.
Wax the bottles, seal them tight,
For the south wind that soothes, for the north wind that bites."

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text:
"How does this fine wine taste to the tongue?
As 'Mondstadt' to the ear: like a sweet dream of freedom.
And what are the fruits that went into the brew?
An explorer's courage, a love tender and true."

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text:
"A defender's will, strong as yesteryear,
Joining the thousand winds in a song of good cheer,
Turning sour into sweet, bitter notes fade away,
As we wait, wait for a windier day."

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text:
"Pray tell, what treasure does this barrel hold?
'Tis wheat's greatest triumph, the true liquid gold.
As it flows from the keg, what sound drifts by?
Wind chimes in the boundless, immemorial sky."

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text:
"We raise up our glasses, and voices in song,
As we wait, wait for the wind to sing along.
Where do we turn once the thousand winds take flight?
To the tales of the lyre, to the sweet dream of tonight."

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Dear friends, let us now open the wines.

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: To the Anemo Archon!

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: To the Anemo Archon...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: To the Anemo Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Umm... There's no wind...

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Don't feel sad, Klee.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: But why didn't he come? If the Anemo God didn't come home... is it because he doesn't like the wine we brought for him?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I don't think so...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course not! You know, Klee, the wind isn't the only form that the Anemo Archon can turn into. He can turn into anything! So today, he must've come back looking like something else!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Huh? Really? Maybe he turned into... a Jumpy Dumpty!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure! Jumpy Dumpty it is! Hope you're listening, Anemo Archon!

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Heehee... Razor, did the Anemo Archon bring you a blessing?

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: I talked a lot with you all, and I learned a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Now, I am not afraid.

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: I think that is a blessing.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Don't forget to save me a glass of your wine once it's finished fermenting!

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Yes. We share together, and we remember together.

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: Yay! But... now I'm getting thirsty...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've all done a lot of talking. Let's go get something to drink, shall we?

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: I heard that the Angel's Share is selling a new drink called "Fruits of the Festival." Everyone's saying it's delicious!

response.speaker: Klee
response.text: I want some, I want some!

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Okay, everyone, let's go.

choices.text: It will remind us of this moment.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Razor, you were sooo cool back there!

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Cool? But inside, I feel warm...

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: No, not like that. When you think something's awesome, you can say it's "cool," or "sweet"!

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Oh... Hmm, but I think Klee is sweet.

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Overall, I think this task was a success...

dialogues.speaker: Noelle
dialogues.text: Oh no! Sucrose's lab equipment! I should go help her carry it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Windcoming Day is finally here. Let's get a move on, or we'll miss the toasting ceremony!
